title: Castateum
summary: Castateum is an Indigenous placename recorded for salt meadows near Flatlands in Brooklyn. The marker represents the broader historic meadow landscape rather than a surveyed tract boundary.
address_label: General Flatlands / Marine Park salt-meadow area, Brooklyn, NY (approximate)
map_geometry_source: Approximate public-land reference point for Tooker's salt meadows near Flatlands; not a reconstructed deed boundary.
why_this_matters: Castateum preserves a Native name for the Flatlands salt-meadow landscape and recalls the ecological and working importance of coastal grasslands before the modern Brooklyn shoreline took shape. The approximate marker keeps that history visible without pretending that the original meadow tract has been precisely surveyed.
introduction_content: Castateum, with recorded forms including Casteteuw and Kestateuw, named one of three salt-meadow flats near Flatlands in early Dutch land records.
history_content: The records distinguish eastern, middle, and western flats. Modern development and shoreline change make those colonial tract boundaries difficult to reconstruct, so the map uses a broad public-land reference point near the remaining salt-marsh landscape.
translation_content: Recorded related forms include Casteteuw, Kestateuw, Cashuteyte, and Kaskutensuken. Tooker interpreted the name as referring to a place where grass was cut or mowed.
whereintheworld_content: The marker is placed broadly in the Flatlands and Marine Park salt-marsh area. It is a representative point for the historic meadow landscape, not an exact parcel boundary.
